To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“the collective of professional players emerges from repeated procedures of player recruitment, selection, and de-selection through all ages of childhood and youth rather from early selection and continuous nurture in talent promotion programmes”.

(1) in German football, the collective of professional football players is built up continuously through childhood and youth, and that (2) the number of players involved in talent promotion is built up continuously throughout childhood and youth.

the collective of German professional players emerged from the repeated procedures of selection of the most promising players and de-selection of the less promising ones through childhood and youth, rather than from early talent identification and long-term nurture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the collective of professional football players and not with the development of individual players.
the question of how the collective of professional football players is built up in a system of TID/TP.
a more differentiated view on the development of elite athletes and on the effectiveness of talent promotion programmes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the German system of TID/TP does not work.

the German system of TID/TP does not seem to be effective in the sense of a systematic and successful selection and nurture of professional players, but rather in the sense of an effective de-selection and release of non-eligible players.
TP is a process rather than a programme, and it is a process of repeated procedures of selection (of players) and de-selection (of players) rather than a process of early selection (of players).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the collective of players who are successful at senior age is not a result of the selection of talented players early in childhood, but of repeated selection processes through all age categories of childhood and youth, and of the development of players in the course of these selection procedures.
there is no evidence that the collective of German professional footballers emerged from the early selection and long term nurture of talent promotion programs.
the collective of players that is needed to achieve success in professional football is built up by a process of selection, de-selection and selection again.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the collective of current Bundesliga players is not the outcome of a long-term nurture in TP programmes, but rather the result of a continuous selection and de-selection process.

TID/TP should not aim at early and long-term nurture but rather at repeated procedures of player identification and selection, which should be based on a combination of objective and subjective criteria.
the development of elite players is a complex process that cannot be reduced to a single factor.
